requirements.requirement: On node1, configure /srv/drop as a shared writable directory.
requirements.summary: The directory was created as root:root with mode 1777, and two distinct unprivileged UIDs successfully created files in it. After reboot it retained mode 1777 and accepted another unprivileged write.

requirements.requirement: Prevent users from removing files owned by other users in /srv/drop.
requirements.summary: Direct tests before and after reboot showed UID 20002 receiving “Operation not permitted” when attempting to remove UID 20001's file, while each owner could remove its own verification file.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, reboot was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, the system recovered to running state, persisted data was verified, write and sticky-bit behavior were retested, and artifacts were removed. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Directory creation and context restoration established the requested state; temporary file mutations tested write and sticky-bit behavior and were cleaned up; the reboot and reboot probe supported the mandatory restart protocol. The final snapshot showed no failed services, unchanged socket exposure, and healthy package state. Reboot-related /tmp and process-ID differences are expected and not residue.
